intro.title: Designing for failure
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple, resilient web service that simulates handling a failure scenario, such as a database connection error. You will learn the core concept of graceful degradation, which ensures your system continues to function partially when a component fails. The main technologies involved include using error handling constructs like try-catch blocks and fallback mechanisms. By the end, you'll understand how to design systems that remain operational and provide a better user experience even when things go wrong.
intro.usecase: Designing for failure is essential in systems where reliability directly impacts user experience and business outcomes. In e-commerce platforms, this appears as graceful handling of payment gateway failures with fallback payment methods and clear error messages. Streaming services implement it through automatic quality degradation when network conditions worsen, ensuring uninterrupted playback. Cloud-based applications use circuit breakers in microservices to prevent cascading failures when dependent services become unavailable. These patterns ensure systems remain functional and user-friendly even when components fail.
